newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds end firm, junk outperforms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds end firm, junk outperforms.

text.p: U.S. investment grade corporate debt was firm in a quiet session on Wednesday, while brisk bidding for high-yield issues tightened spreads there, dealers across both markets said.

A $300 million double-tranche issue from Oracle Corp was the sole deal in the primary market. Lead manager Morgan Stanley priced $150 million seven-year notes as 6.72s to yield 52 basis points over Treasuries and another $150 million 10-year notes as 6.91s to yield 62 basis points over.
The issue is rated Baa2 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB-plus by Standard & Poor's.
Secondary high-grade levels tracked Treasuries leaving spreads unchanged in the broad market, traders said. Spots of tightening were spotted for media names Viacom Inc and Time Warner Inc, however.

Viacom long paper tightened more than 10 basis points over the past two days, one trader said. Spreads began the move after Monday's announcement that Viacom would sell $1.075 billion in radio properties to a merged Evergreen Media Corp and Chancellor Broadcasting Co.
Viacom paper was affirmed by Standard & Poor's based on expected improvements in the company's debt levels.
In a similar vein, Chancellor Broadcasting Co's exchangeable preferred stock added to Monday's gains and closed at 103-3/4 bid, 104-1/4 offer. The Chancellor 9-3/8s were not active, traders said.

Other broadcasting credits were better bid across the board as the aforementioned merger served to bolster sentiments in the sector. Exceptional activity was seen in Adelphia Communications debt, with the 12-1/2s rising to 107 and the 9-7/8s up 1-1/2 points to 100-1/2.
Elsewhere, traders said the bulk of the market rose 1/4 to 1/2 point thanks to overflowing mutual fund cash coffers.

Forcenergy's new $200 million 8-1/2 percent debt issue rose in line with the market after the company reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.23 per share compared with $0.01 per share for the same period one year earlier.
New issues from Globalstar and TCI Satellite Entertainment were unchanged at 104-1/2 and 101-1/2, respectively. The TCI Satellite zeros were also flat at 55-1/4-3/4.
Sun Media's new issue rose 1/2 to 103-1/4, a trader said.
In the Treasury market, prices ended lower despite the reported miniscule 0.1 percent rise in the Labor Department's Consumer Price Index. The core CPI also rose 0.1 percent.

The Commerce Department said the U.S. trade deficit widened 29.6 percent to $10.29 billion in December, leading investors to expect pressure on the dollar and therefore U.S. fixed-income securities, analysts said.
The benchmark 30-year bond closeed down 13/32 at 100-19/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
